etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English composen, from Old French composer (“to compose, compound, adjust, settle”), from com- + poser, as an adaptation of Latin componere (“to put together, compose”), from com- (“together”) + ponere (“to put, place”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To make something by merging parts. [from later 15th c.]

quote.citation: December 22 1678, Thomas Sprat, A Sermon Preached before the King at White-Hall
quote.text: Zeal ought to be composed of the highest degrees of all pious affection.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To make up the whole; to constitute.

quote.citation: 1741, I[saac] Watts, The Improvement of the Mind: Or, A Supplement to the Art of Logick: […], London:  […]  James Brackstone, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: A few useful things  […]  compose their intellectual possessions.

definitions.definition: (transitive or intransitive) To construct by mental labor; to think up; particularly, to produce or create a literary or musical work.

quote.citation: 1714, Alexander Pope, Imitation of Horace, Book II. Sat. 6:
quote.text: Let me  […]  compose / Something in Verse as true as Prose.

quote.citation: 1838, Benjamin Haydon, Painting, and the fine arts:
quote.text: the genius that composed such works as the "Standard" and "Last Supper"

definitions.definition: (sometimes reflexive) To calm; to free from agitation.

quote.citation: 1697, Virgil, “(please specify the book number)”, in John Dryden, transl., The Works of Virgil: Containing His Pastorals, Georgics, and Æneis. […], London:  […]  Jacob Tonson, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Compose thy mind; / Nor frauds are here contrived, nor force designed.

definitions.definition: To arrange the elements of a photograph or other picture.
To settle (an argument, dispute etc.); to come to a settlement.

quote.citation: 2010, Christopher Hitchens, Hitch-22, Atlantic, published 2011, page 280:
quote.text: By trying his best to compose matters with the mullahs, he had sincerely shown that he did not seek a violent collision  […]

definitions.definition: To arrange in proper form; to reduce to order; to put in proper state or condition.

quote.citation: 1697, Virgil, “(please specify the book number)”, in John Dryden, transl., The Works of Virgil: Containing His Pastorals, Georgics, and Æneis. […], London:  […]  Jacob Tonson, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: In a peaceful grave my corpse compose.

quote.citation: 1667, John Milton, “Book II”, in Paradise Lost. […], London:  […]  [Samuel Simmons], and are to be sold by Peter Parker […]; [a]nd by Robert Boulter […]; [a]nd Matthias Walker, […], →OCLC; republished as Paradise Lost in Ten Books: […], London: Basil Montagu Pickering […], 1873, →OCLC:
quote.text: How in safety best we may / Compose our present evils.

definitions.definition: (printing, dated) To arrange (types) in a composing stick for printing; to typeset.
